# Commands

<!-- generated by scripts/docs/generate-reference.py from the code; do not edit by hand -->

Every command of `stratarc`, generated from the command line parser so the page cannot drift from the code. Run `python3 scripts/docs/generate-reference.py --check` to confirm it still matches.

## Global Options

Global options are accepted before or after the command.

| option | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--root` `PATH` | the source root (sets STRATARC_SOURCE) |
| `--home` `PATH` | the home directory the runtime targets hang under (sets STRATARC_HOME) |
| `--projects-root` `PATH` | the directory that holds project checkouts (sets STRATARC_PROJECTS_DIR) |
| `--json` | print one JSON envelope instead of text |
| `--debug` | print a traceback when a command stops unexpectedly |

## Exit Statuses

| status | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | ok |
| 1 | failure: the command ran and did not succeed |
| 2 | invalid input: a bad argument, an unknown source root, an invalid `stratarc.toml`, or a refusal by the engine |
| 3 | denied: the home is missing or not writable |
| 4 | conflict: the target already holds something |
| 5 | unavailable: a packaged resource is missing, a file in the home is newer than this stratarc, an adapter does not support the installed runtime, or the change log database is locked |
| 6 | drift: the deployed files differ from what the source renders |
| 130 | interrupted |

## `help`

explain one command, or list them all.

```text
stratarc help [COMMAND]
```

| argument | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `COMMAND` | The command to explain. |

## `setup`

walk through creating a source root, choosing runtimes and the first deploy.

```text
usage: stratarc components [-h] [--manifest MANIFEST] [--list]

options:
  -h, --help           show this help message and exit
  --manifest MANIFEST  manifest to read (default: <source
                       root>/components.json)
  --list               print what is declared

examples:
  stratarc components                                   validate the manifest
  stratarc components --list                            validate, then list each component
  stratarc components --manifest ./components.json      validate a manifest at another path
```

## `init`

scaffold a new source root into TARGET.

```text
stratarc init target
```

| argument | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `target` | Directory to create; must be absent or empty. |

## `doctor`

report the health of the install, the home and the source root.

```text
stratarc doctor [--permissions] [--clean] [--yes] [--report]
```

| option | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--permissions` | Also print what each command reads and writes. |
| `--clean` | Also list the old backups and cache the home can shed. |
| `--yes` | With --clean, remove what it lists. |
| `--report` | Also write a redacted bundle for an issue report under state/debug. |

## `sync`

render the source into every enabled runtime and managed project.

```text
stratarc sync [--verify] [--rollback-on-drift] [--only RUNTIME] [--dry-run] [--list]
```

| option | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--verify` | After the write, verify the change against what is deployed; exit 6 on drift. |
| `--rollback-on-drift` | When verification finds drift, restore the runtime files from the home backups (implies --verify). |
| `--only` `RUNTIME` | Sync one runtime and skip project delivery. |
| `--dry-run` | Print what a sync would change and write nothing. |
| `--list` | List the runtimes and whether each target exists. |

## `check`

report what is out of date, write nothing, exit 6 on drift.

```text
stratarc check [--only RUNTIME]
```

| option | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--only` `RUNTIME` | Check one runtime. |

## `diff`

print what a sync would change, write nothing, exit 0.

```text
stratarc diff [--only RUNTIME]
```

| option | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--only` `RUNTIME` | Diff one runtime. |


## `validate`

check a source root against the schemas and the engine's rules.

```text
usage: stratarc validate [-h] [--root ROOT] [--strict]
                         [--checks {generic,private,all}]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --root ROOT           source root (default: the resolved source root)
  --strict              exit 1 when any error-level finding exists
  --checks {generic,private,all}
                        which class of checks to run (default: all)

examples:
  stratarc validate                          report every finding, exit 0
  stratarc validate --strict                 exit 1 when any error is found
  stratarc validate --checks generic --root ~/agent-source
                                             run only the built in checks on another root
```

## `projects`

deliver projects-root/ into the managed project checkouts.

```text
usage: stratarc projects [-h] [--check] [--only NAME] [--adopt NAME]
                         [--verify] [--new NAME] [--checkout PATH]
                         [--remote OWNER/REPO] [--public] [--workflows]
                         [--dry-run] [--registry-check] [--root PATH]

options:
  -h, --help           show this help message and exit
  --check              dry run: print what each project would receive, write
                       nothing, exit 1 if any project is stale
  --only NAME          deliver only NAME, the name of its directory under
                       projects-root, instead of every project
  --adopt NAME         first time capture: copy project NAME's existing
                       checkout config into projects-root/NAME/, then exit
  --verify             report manifest and filesystem disagreement, exit 1 if
                       any
  --new NAME           load a new project NAME: copy the source root's project
                       template to its root folder, add its row and column to
                       the control plane and its slug to the registries, add
                       the .gitignore block and local/ folder to its checkout,
                       then check it; safe to repeat; with --check or --dry-
                       run it writes nothing; it never delivers config (that
                       stays with `stratarc sync`)
  --checkout PATH      with --new: the project's checkout (default:
                       active/NAME under the projects root)
  --remote OWNER/REPO  with --new: the project's GitHub slug, recorded in
                       remotes.json and as the origin in the control plane
  --public             with --new: the project is a public repository; list it
                       in public-targets.json and give it no configuration
  --workflows          with --new: also copy the source root's optional
                       workflows.toml project template, if it has one
  --dry-run            with --new: the same as --check
  --registry-check     read only: report a control plane project without a
                       root folder or a remotes.json entry, a root folder not
                       in the control plane, and a public project with a row,
                       one per line, exit 1 if any
  --root PATH          the source root to deliver from (default:
                       $STRATARC_SOURCE, then the nearest stratarc.toml, then
                       the current directory)

examples:
  stratarc projects                       deliver every project
  stratarc projects --check               show what would change, exit 1 if stale
  stratarc projects --only my-project     deliver one project
  stratarc projects --adopt my-project    capture an existing checkout's config
                                          into projects-root/my-project/
  stratarc projects --new my-project --remote owner/my-project
                                          load a new project: root, control plane, registries
  stratarc projects --registry-check      check the control plane against the roots and registries
```

## `gen-rules-digest`

render or check the rules digest in instruction files.

```text
usage: stratarc gen-rules-digest [-h] (--print | --embed FILE [FILE ...] |
                                 --check FILE [FILE ...])
                                 [--rules-root RULES_ROOT] [--prefix PREFIX]
                                 [--source-root SOURCE_ROOT] [--column COLUMN]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --print               Write the rendered digest block to stdout.
  --embed FILE [FILE ...]
                        Replace the marker-delimited digest in each FILE.
  --check FILE [FILE ...]
                        Exit non-zero if any FILE's digest has drifted.
  --rules-root RULES_ROOT
                        Rule tree to render (default: $RULES_DIGEST_SOURCE,
                        else the source root's rules/, which carries
                        tiers.json).
  --prefix PREFIX       Text the Full rule: pointers open with (default:
                        ${STRATARC_SOURCE}/rules/, or the rules/ directory of
                        --source-root when given).
  --source-root SOURCE_ROOT
                        Render for this checkout: every ${STRATARC_SOURCE} in
                        the digest and in each target becomes this path.
                        Deploy time only; the committed AGENTS.md keeps the
                        token.
  --column COLUMN       Render this control-plane.md column's opt-ins instead
                        of the global tier plus the common tier. Read from the
                        source root's control-plane.md.

examples:
  stratarc gen-rules-digest --print                  show the digest
  stratarc gen-rules-digest --embed AGENTS.md        refresh the digest in AGENTS.md
  stratarc gen-rules-digest --check AGENTS.md        exit non-zero if it drifted (for CI)
```

## `components`

validate components.json and list what it declares.

```text
usage: stratarc components [-h] [--manifest MANIFEST] [--list]

options:
  -h, --help           show this help message and exit
  --manifest MANIFEST  manifest to read (default: <source
                       root>/components.json)
  --list               print what is declared

examples:
  stratarc components                                   validate the manifest
  stratarc components --list                            validate, then list each component
  stratarc components --manifest ./components.json      validate a manifest at another path
```

## `drift`

report where checkouts differ from what the control plane delivers.

```text
usage: stratarc drift [-h] [--format {text,json}] [--report] [--here]
                      [--staged] [--repo] [--source] [--root PATH]
                      {explain} ...

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --format {text,json}  output format (default: text)
  --report              also write a Markdown report and a dated copy under
                        the state home
  --here                session start mode: check only the checkout holding
                        the current folder, print one line when it has
                        findings, always exit 0
  --staged              pre-commit mode: check only the staged files of the
                        checkout holding the current folder, exit 1 on an
                        error level finding
  --repo                project CI mode: check the whole checkout holding the
                        current folder with no source root, exit 1 on an error
                        level finding
  --source              control plane CI mode: check the source root alone
                        with no checkouts, exit 1 on an error level finding
  --root PATH           the source root (default: $STRATARC_SOURCE, then the
                        nearest stratarc.toml, then the current directory)

examples:
  stratarc drift
  stratarc drift --format json
  stratarc drift --report
  stratarc drift --here
  stratarc drift explain docs/guide/AGENTS.md
```

## `adapter`

manage the translators from the source to a runtime.

```text
stratarc adapter {list,show,remove,register,add,new,status,deprecate}
```

### `adapter list`

list adapters.

```text
stratarc adapter list
```

### `adapter show`

show one adapter's manifest.

```text
stratarc adapter show name
```

| argument | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | The adapter name. |

### `adapter remove`

remove a registered manifest; a bundled adapter reverts to its derived one.

```text
stratarc adapter remove name
```

| argument | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | The adapter name. |

### `adapter register`

record the runtime versions an adapter supports, from a manifest path or package; the adapter itself is adapters/<name>.py in the source root.

```text
stratarc adapter register path-or-package [--replace]
```

| argument | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `path-or-package` | A manifest.json file, a directory holding one, or an installed package that ships one. |

| option | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--replace` | Replace a manifest that is already registered. |

### `adapter add`

the same as register.

```text
stratarc adapter add path-or-package [--replace]
```

| argument | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `path-or-package` | A manifest.json file, a directory holding one, or an installed package that ships one. |

| option | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--replace` | Replace a manifest that is already registered. |

### `adapter new`

write a starting adapter for a runtime into the source root's adapters directory.

```text
stratarc adapter new name [--target DIR]
```

| argument | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | The runtime name: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. |

| option | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--target` `DIR` | The runtime's directory under the home (default: .<name>). |

### `adapter status`

compare each adapter with the installed runtime.

```text
stratarc adapter status [--runtime-version RUNTIME=VERSION]
```

| option | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--runtime-version` `RUNTIME=VERSION` | Override a detected runtime version. Repeatable. |

### `adapter deprecate`

mark an adapter as no longer supported (needs --reason and --end-date).

```text
stratarc adapter deprecate name --reason REASON --end-date YYYY-MM-DD [--replacement REPLACEMENT]
```

| argument | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | The adapter name. |

| option | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--reason` `REASON` | Required: why it is deprecated. |
| `--end-date` `YYYY-MM-DD` | Required: the last day it is supported. |
| `--replacement` `REPLACEMENT` | The adapter to use instead. |
